newsitem.title: USA: Autumn Jackson won't take test -- lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Autumn Jackson won't take test -- lawyer.

text.p: The woman convicted of extorting $40 million from entertainer Bill Cosby will not submit to a blood test to determine if he is her father, MSNBC reported Tuesday.
"We won't respond to some grandstanding move," said an attorney for Autumn Jackson's mother in an interview with the cable news network.
Cosby's lawyer said on Monday the entertainer had given blood for a test to determine if he is Jackson's father.
The lawyer, Jack Schmitt, challenged Jackson and her mother, Shawn Thompson, to take similar tests.
The mother's attorney, Wanda Akin, said the decision was reached with Jackson's attorney, Robert Baum.

"It's interesting that at this juncture in the game that that's what Mr. Cosby wants to do, and I don't think it's based on any sincerity to get closer to this situation but it is a move to distance himself," Akin said on MSNBC.

Jackson, 22, was convicted last Friday in New York of threatening to go to a tabloid newspaper with her story unless Cosby paid her $40 million. Her attorney has said she grew up believing Cosby was her father.
The actor has admitted having an affair with Jackson's mother and paid for the young woman's education.
The judge in the federal extortion case ruled out any discussion of Cosby's paternity as irrelevant.
She faces up to 12 years in prison when she is sentenced.
